scope: All 32 mapped Grands-Échezeaux parcels inventoried; all nine recorded right holders revisited at Tier 2. Nineteen selected free company filings (804 pages), published whole-cru holdings and all seven Winehog vineyard-article previews reviewed. Seven parcels have exact-reference filing evidence. No verified current farmer; not an exhaustive search of every archive.
rules: Candidate names are research hypotheses, never verified farmers.
Rights as of 2025-01-01, modern cadastral geometry and estate descriptions are different evidence.
A reviewed-at date or webpage crawl date is not a farming date.
Unmatched rights do not mean no owner or no farmer.
A cru intersection does not establish that the whole cadastral parcel is planted or farmed.
No automatic assignment from area, adjacency, named area, wine bottler, manager or similar company name.
Company filings record contributions and dated lease recitals; lease mandates are not proof of execution or current operation.
Research dates come from an explicitly selected source; supporting registry dates never fill an undated research source.
Disputed named-area locations are alternatives and contribute nothing to definite climat totals.
Literal printed references without accepted lineage, and historical holdings without confirmed continuation, do not become current parcel assignments.

accessGaps: Tier 2 reviewed all nine holder groups via free filing indexes and 19 selected filings (804 pages); this is not an exhaustive reading of every corporate archive. Paid land-registry copies and outreach remain Tier 3.

Private individuals are absent from the legal-entity file: 13 parcels (2.06 ha of the cru) have no matched company record. Published holdings compare whole named-area totals and do not assign those parcels.

No current parcel-specific executed lease plus actual-operation evidence was found. Anne’s intended 2021 lease end, Lamarche’s planned 2019 termination and the Mongeard GFA statutory leasing requirement do not prove execution or current farming.

SEPV’s D103 contribution schedule is resolved, but no cru-specific current lease to Maison Joseph Drouhin was found. Its 2019/2020 guide holding is 0.47 ha versus Morris’s 0.48; the current estate page states no holding area.
Liger-Belair’s reported 2022 métayage arrangement and the April 2026 suspended application remain separate. No later decision or evidence of who farms D0615/D0616 meanwhile was found.

The Modot legal identity crosswalk to SIREN 778173500 is supported, but its provisional DGFiP identifier and unprovable historical identifier continuity are retained. Schenk/Villamont group context does not supply a land lease.

Villamont publishes approximately 0.5 ha and a separate 16-are sheet; the older guide gives 0.43 ha. No dated change or scope explanation resolves these figures. Noëllat’s 0.30/0.38/0.40-ha figures are also unresolved.

The Eugénie planting schedule’s literal D11 remains unmatched. The Millot estate timeline (1986) conflicts with Winehog’s tentative first-harvest inference (1997); neither gives current cadastral references.
The SA Mongeard filings do not supply the named 2023 conveyance for D0681. DVF records its sale without party names; a later company record is not proof of the original buyer or farmer.

All seven Grands-Échezeaux vineyard articles in the Winehog index were read to their public boundary. Six restrict detailed parcel discussion to subscribers. The free DRC aerial was read but contains no cadastral numbers; subscriber-only parcel maps were not accessed.

The Dreyfus Ashby Drouhin importer PDF returned HTTP 403; the free estate sheet was reviewed instead. The live Vinous 2022 review returned only a loading shell; the free Decanter table supplies the reported métayage fact. Search snippets are not treated as retrieved articles.

The quoted 2017 magazine owner list and original 1855/1892 guide volumes were not independently retrieved. Kohut’s separate current holding and Gros Frère et Sœur’s actual last harvest remain unconfirmed.

Notices outside the regional (2019–2026) and departmental (2016–2020) bulletins, and pre-2016 bulletins, were not searched. Cadastral lineage covers 2019–2026; DVF+ runs from January 2014 to November 2025 and names no party.
